<!-- The fronts are computed by zeno: python3 site/gen_fronts.py writes instances/fronts.json and
     instances/_catalogue.md (the sections below). js/catalogue.js draws the cards. -->

Each card below plots the Pareto front of one instance as computed by zeno: cost on the horizontal
axis, makespan on the vertical one, and a staircase through the front's points. Moving right along
the staircase trades a higher cost for a shorter makespan. Hover a point for its values, or
*Enlarge* a card for a larger plot and the table of its points. A card names the instance as its
suite does and gives the arguments zeno runs, from which any front can be recomputed:

```bash
build/release/zeno -n 10 -t 8 -p 3 -C 3 -D 3
```

The instances come from the regression tests (the golden instances), the benchmark suites, and a
few metric instances whose cities are random points in the plane or on a sphere. How they are
built is documented on the sub-pages:

- [Model and data files](model.qmd): what an instance is, and the 2-line and 3-line data files.
- [Generator](generator.qmd): the families `-C`, `-D`, `-E`, `-W`, and the scale options.
- [PDDL](pddl.qmd): the domain file and the problems `zeno pddl` writes.
- [Benchmark and golden suites](suites.qmd): the suite files and what each one measures.
- [Instances with known fronts](known-fronts.qmd): closed forms and fronts checked by an
  exhaustive oracle.
- [Size guidance](sizing.qmd): how large an instance zeno solves, and what drives the time.

All instances here but one are symmetric, and their fronts are exact. The non-symmetric metric
instance (`--hubs apart`) is marked *bracket*: zeno prints the plans it achieves and reports on its
standard error which gaps its lower bounds certify; for this instance they do not certify them all.

::: {#zs-catalogue data-zs-fronts="fronts.json"}
